item.title: Linux: The Foundation of Modern DevOps
item.description:
Linux: The Foundation of Modern DevOps

Linux powers nearly everything on the Internet.

Whether you browse a website, stream a movie, deploy an application, or use cloud services, chances are Linux is running somewhere in the background.

If you want to become a DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer, Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), Platform Engineer, or Backend Developer, Linux is the first skill you should master.

This guide explains Linux from the ground up with practical examples and projects.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Managing Swap Space and Swappiness in Linux Mint
item.description:
The Ultimate Guide to Managing Swap Space and Swappiness in Linux Mint

If your system runs low on physical RAM, Linux utilizes Swap memory as a safety net. Swap acts as a extension of your system’s RAM by allocating space on your storage drive (SSD or HDD). When physical memory is saturated, the kernel offloads inactive memory pages into swap, keeping your desktop responsive and preventing application crashes caused by Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors.

item.title: Troubleshooting Linux Boot Failures and Optimizing Linux Mint Performance
item.description:
Dealing with boot errors can be daunting, but Linux gives you full control to inspect, repair, and optimize your system. In this comprehensive guide, we cover how to fix missing EFI bootloaders, format and rebuild GRUB from scratch using live environment tools, and squeeze maximum performance out of Linux Mint.

Part 1: Resolving the “failed to open /efi/ubuntu not found” Error

When your system fails to boot and displays the error failed to open /efi/ubuntu not found, it means the UEFI firmware or GRUB bootloader cannot locate the necessary EFI binaries to start the OS. This typically occurs after major Windows updates in dual-boot setups, disk partition changes, or corrupted EFI filesystems.
